level1.text: A ceiling lamp hangs at rest from a vertical cord. The weight of the lamp is $18\,\text{N}$. How large is the tension of the cord on the lamp?
In a tug of war the rope is at rest. Team A pulls the rope to the left with a force of $850\,\text{N}$. The weight of the rope is ignored. With what force does team B pull the rope to the right?
A skater stands on the ice and pushes the board of the rink with the hands with a force of $90\,\text{N}$. With what force does the board push the skater?

A car drives along a straight road at constant velocity. The road pushes the driving wheels of the car forwards with a force of $620\,\text{N}$, and the air resistance on the car is $380\,\text{N}$. In addition, rolling resistance acts backwards on the car. How large is the rolling resistance?
A book of mass $0.65\,\text{kg}$ rests on a table. The Earth pulls the book with a force equal to its weight. With what force does the book pull the Earth?

level2.text: On a table there is a book of weight $8.0\,\text{N}$ and on top of it another book of weight $5.0\,\text{N}$. The books are at rest. With what force does the lower book press the table?

A swimmer swims straight in the horizontal direction at constant velocity. Her weight is $720\,\text{N}$ and the buoyancy of the water is equally large. She pushes the water backwards with her hands and feet with an average force of $65\,\text{N}$. How large is the average drag of the water on the swimmer?

A skydiver whose mass with equipment is $85\,\text{kg}$ descends straight down at constant velocity with the parachute open. How large is the air resistance on the skydiver and the parachute together?

The weight of an elevator car is $5.8\,\text{kN}$, and the car contains passengers whose total mass is $320\,\text{kg}$. The elevator rises at constant velocity. How large is the tension of the cable on the car? Answer in kilonewtons.

level3.text: A hot-air balloon descends straight down at constant velocity. The combined weight of the balloon, the hot air inside it, the basket and the passengers is $4.62\,\text{kN}$, and the buoyancy of the surrounding air is $4.35\,\text{kN}$. How large is the air resistance on the balloon, and in which direction does it point? Give the magnitude in kilonewtons and the direction in words; only the magnitude is checked.

Two identical ring magnets are threaded onto a vertical wooden stick standing on a table. The magnets repel each other, and the upper one floats at rest above the lower one without touching it. The weight of each magnet is $0.30\,\text{N}$, and friction against the stick is ignored. With what force does the table support the lower magnet? The force of the stick is ignored.

Two spring scales are hung one below the other: the upper one is attached to the ceiling, and the lower one hangs from the hook of the upper one. An apple of weight $1.5\,\text{N}$ hangs from the hook of the lower scale. The weight of the lower scale itself is $0.40\,\text{N}$. Everything is at rest. What does the upper scale show?
